title: How Mustang Modules Share Messages
introduction:
Your Mustang’s electronic modules share information instead of each demanding a private wire for every message. I picture a shared conversation: commands, status reports and data travel between modules, while a gateway helps messages reach the diagnostic scan tool.

This overview explains which networks connect to the diagnostic connector and which communicate through the gateway. It is a map of communication paths, without electrical test instructions or fault limits.

edits.why: Separate the shared-message principle from the route a diagnostic tool uses to reach each network.

edits.text: Multiplexing sends 2 or more signals simultaneously over a single circuit. It lets 2 or more electronic modules, called nodes, exchange messages over a twisted wire pair identified as data (+) and data (-). Those messages carry commands, status or data. Sharing the wiring reduces redundant components and electrical wiring, helping reduce vehicle weight.
edits.why: Think of a shared conversation rather than a separate telephone line for every message. The modules can exchange information without duplicating every sensor or wiring route.
